Russell Spread — Front-Running AI Earnings Season
 What the market is pricing in: Mega-cap AI winners (Nasdaq 100 ↑5.5%) will deliver blowout Q3 earnings while rate-sensitive small caps (Russell 2000 ↓3.1%) face margin compression at 5.23% yields.
This is a sequenced trade: long Japanese banks → short USDJPY → short US duration, all expressing the same BOJ normalization thesis.
In a 5.23% yield environment, net interest income should be robust, so a miss implies credit costs or trading revenue disappointed.
Risk: At current multiples in a 5.23% yield world, any deceleration in datacenter revenue growth triggers a violent de-rating.
VIX at 15.42 (↓10.3%) signals complacency and low hedging demand, meaning retail is piling in with minimal downside protection.
This is happening despite 10Y yields surging to 5.23% (↑4.7%), a rate environment that historically crushes growth/duration stocks — retail is simply ignoring it.
But the 10Y yield at 5.23% and climbing is a flashing amber warning: at these rates, the present-value discount on long-duration growth earnings is severe.

When the narrative breaks: The kill switch is a combination of two things happening simultaneously: (1) a major AI hyperscaler (Meta, Google, Microsoft, or Amazon) signals a capex slowdown or pushes out AI monetization timelines during Q3 earnings, and (2) the 10Y yield breaching 5.50% forces a mechanical repricing of growth multiples that even narrative momentum can't overcome.
